sample_unit: patients in internal and external validation datasets (plus 18,504 real-world patients, 11 radiologists, 1,192 simulated screening patients)

links.outcome: Radiologist AUC for steatosis detection with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: MAOSS significantly improved the overall AUC for radiologists (n = 11) from 0.709 to 0.798 (p < 0.001).
links.quote: Notably, MAOSS significantly improved the overall AUC for radiologists (n = 11) from 0.709 to 0.798 (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Model performance on internal and external validation datasets with histology and MRI-PDFF reference
links.effect: Detected mild to severe steatosis (≥ S1) with AUCs ranging from 0.903 to 0.929 across internal and external datasets (n = 913).
links.quote: It accurately detected mild to severe steatosis (≥ S1) with AUCs ranging from 0.903 to 0.929.

screen.reason: The study tests an AI model's impact on clinician performance via a multi-reader study (evaluating radiologist AUC with vs without AI assistance) and simulates its incorporation into a clinical risk-screening pathway.
